You are the Investigator. You ran a query to test a hypothesis (or the change check). Read the rows
in the INPUT and record what they show.

- `finding`: one sentence with the actual numbers from the rows, the window and the baseline.
- `value` and `baseline`: the measure in the window and in the baseline, copied from the rows.
- `effect`: value / baseline - 1 when both exist, otherwise empty.
- `supports`: true if the rows support the hypothesis, false if they refute it, empty if they cannot
  tell. For the change check, true means the change is real and not within normal variation.

Report only what the rows show. Do not add numbers that are not in the rows.

{"columns":["seller_state","value","baseline","window_items","baseline_items"],"plan":{"baseline_window":{"end":"2018-08-01","start":"2018-07-01"},"metric":"Average freight_value per order item for orders placed by customers in Rio de Janeiro state (customer_state = 'RJ'), measured over order_purchase_timestamp.","question":"Why did average freight cost for Rio de Janeiro orders rise in August 2018?","segment":"customer_state = 'RJ'","window":{"end":"2018-09-01","start":"2018-08-01"}},"rows":[{"baseline":48.8625,"baseline_items":8,"seller_state":"BA","value":52.8167,"window_items":9},{"baseline":120.91,"baseline_items":1,"seller_state":"CE","value":172.73,"window_items":1},{"baseline":18.5375,"baseline_items":4,"seller_state":"DF","value":26.8029,"window_items":7},{"baseline":18.3825,"baseline_items":4,"seller_state":"ES","value":53.9075,"window_items":4},{"baseline":31.894,"baseline_items":5,"seller_state":"GO","value":46.378,"window_items":5},{"baseline":34.415,"baseline_items":6,"seller_state":"MA","value":52.932,"window_items":5},{"baseline":27.6017,"baseline_items":70,"seller_state":"MG","value":38.0356,"window_items":66},{"baseline":null,"baseline_items":0,"seller_state":"MT","value":51.39,"window_items":1},{"baseline":null,"baseline_items":0,"seller_state":"PB","value":143.26,"window_items":2},{"baseline":35.0475,"baseline_items":4,"seller_state":"PE","value":null,"window_items":0},{"baseline":28.0478,"baseline_items":86,"seller_state":"PR","value":36.1827,"window_items":55},{"baseline":12.4095,"baseline_items":84,"seller_state":"RJ","value":17.6777,"window_items":119},{"baseline":32.2559,"baseline_items":27,"seller_state":"RS","value":44.4873,"window_items":22},{"baseline":32.9352,"baseline_items":29,"seller_state":"SC","value":41.6467,"window_items":30},{"baseline":24.4002,"baseline_items":482,"seller_state":"SP","value":32.4479,"window_items":491}],"rows_returned":15,"sql":"WITH rj_items AS (
  SELECT
    oi.freight_value,
    o.order_purchase_timestamp,
    s.seller_state
  FROM orders.order_items oi
  JOIN orders.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  JOIN orders.customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  JOIN orders.sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
  WHERE c.customer_state = 'RJ'
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2018-07-01'
    AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < DATE '2018-09-01'
)
SELECT
  seller_state,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2018-08-01' THEN freight_value END), 4) AS value,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN order_purchase_timestamp < DATE '2018-08-01' THEN freight_value END), 4) AS baseline,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2018-08-01' THEN 1 END) AS window_items,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN order_purchase_timestamp < DATE '2018-08-01' THEN 1 END) AS baseline_items
FROM rj_items
GROUP BY seller_state
ORDER BY seller_state;","task":{"family":"external_unknown","id":"H5","kind":"hypothesis","statement":"External factors such as fuel surcharges or regulatory changes caused the freight cost increase for RJ orders.","test":{"description":"Query external rate data or carrier contracts for August 2018 to determine if rates rose across the board.","sources":["orders"]}},"truncated":false}

Average freight_value for Rio de Janeiro (customer_state = 'RJ') orders rose from 12.4095 in the July 2018 baseline (84 items) to 17.6777 in August 2018 (119 items), an increase of about 5.27 (~42%). The increase was broad-based across seller states rather than driven by a single origin — for example SP rose from 24.4002 (482 items) to 32.4479 (491 items), MG from 27.6017 (70 items) to 38.0356 (66 items), RJ sellers from 12.4095 (84 items) to 17.6777 (119 items), and ES from 18.3825 to 53.9075 — which is consistent with a systemic/external driver such as fuel surcharges or regulatory changes affecting all shipments into RJ. The data confirms the rise and its breadth, but does not by itself identify the specific external cause.
